recentItems.title: Live: AfD holds press conference after historic election result | DW News
recentItems.description:
Germany's far-right AfD is celebrating after emerging as the strongest force in the Saxony-Anhalt state election. But despite a historic result, the party appears to have fallen short of the outright majority needed to govern alone.
What happens next? Who could shape the next state government? And what does the result mean for German politics?
Join DW's live coverage as we bring you the latest election results, analysis from our political experts, reactions from party leaders, and live updates from the AfD press conference in Berlin and the state capital, Magdeburg.

recentItems.title: Live: What the AfD's big win in Saxony-Anhalt really means? | DW News
recentItems.description:
Germany's Alternative for Germany party has won a overwhelming victory in a regional election being watched right across the nation and the world. The far-right party has claimed 43.8% of the vote in Germany's eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt according to the latest preliminary official results, but is still short of the outright majority it needs to take power. Join DW's Biresh Banerjee and Anja Kueppers-Mckinnon as they discuss this watershed moment and what happens next.

recentItems.title: Official results: Far-right party wins Saxony-Anhalt state elections | DW News
recentItems.description:
The Alternative for Germany has clinched an historic victory in a state election. Preliminary results show the AfD won almost 44 percent of the Sunday vote in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, which puts a far-right party within reach of power at the state level for the first time since the Second World War. But the result is shy of an outright majority - and the AfD may have to find coalition forces. The party wants strict immigration curbs, warmer ties with Russia and less support for Ukraine. DW's Ben Fajzullin speaks to DW political correspondent Giulia Saudelli in Magdeburg about what comes next.

recentItems.title: AfD dominates Saxony-Anhalt: A turning point for Germany? | DW News
recentItems.description:
The AfD has emerged as the dominant force in Saxony-Anhalt, but election victories do not automatically translate into political power. What drove voters to back the party, and what does the result mean for Germany's political future?

Brent Goff speaks with political correspondents Matthew Moore and Bernd Riegert, DW Berlin bureau chief Max Hofmann, and historian and author Katja Hoyer. They break down the results, reactions from party headquarters, the challenge of forming a government, the pressure on Chancellor Friedrich Merz and the wider implications for German politics.
